Subject: ACME POC — Post-call recap & next steps

Thanks for the time today — good discussion. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment before kickoff:

Summary from call:
- Goal: Run a short POC to validate latency, quality, and cost for Acme's customer support summarization flow.
- Primary success criteria: >= 90% coverage of target intents, average quality score >= 2.5/3 on rubric, and median 95th percentile latency < 350ms on target infra.

Proposed evaluation approach (high level):
1) Offline eval (dev set): we run a 1,000-sample offline evaluation using a labeled dev set from Acme. Scoring will be per-example using the rubric (accuracy/faithfulness, fluency, safety, and latency).
2) Human review: a small blinded panel (Acme + Redwood) will do qualitative checks on failure cases.
3) Shadowing: a 1-week low-volume shadow in production (no user-visible changes, rate-limited) to surface real-world distribution and infra metrics.

Timeline (proposal):
- Week of Oct 12: Kickoff + data handoff (Acme provides sample set + schema).
- Week of Oct 19: Offline eval run (2 business days for initial run, then review).
- Week of Oct 26: Shadow/online validation (1 week).
- First week of Nov: Decision point and next steps (scale / rollout).

Ownership:
- Acme: Priya Shah — data lead (provides dataset, access to metrics).
- Redwood: Marissa Cole — eval lead; Dylan Brooks — engagement owner / escalation

Attachments: ACME_POC_eval_template.xlsx (sample schema & data checklist)

Ask: Please confirm the success criteria above and whether Oct 12 kickoff works. Also confirm who at Acme will be the primary reviewer for the offline rubric.

Thanks,

Subject: RE: ACME POC — Post-call recap & next steps (eval methodology)

Dylan — drafting the detailed eval methodology here so we can attach and send to Acme. Feel free to push back on any items.

Offline eval (recommended minimums):
- Sample size: target 1,000 labeled examples. We can run an initial pass with 500 to unblock, but statistical confidence will be lower — we'll mark lower confidence results and recommend expanding to 1,000 before final decision.
- Dev split: stratify by channel and intent to ensure coverage (support email, chat, top 8 intents).
- Metrics & rubric (per-example, 0-3 scoring):
  - Accuracy / Task completion (0: incorrect, 1: partial, 2: mostly correct, 3: perfect)
  - Fluency / Readability (0-3)
  - Safety / Policy compliance (0-3) — automatic policy checks + reviewer override
  - Latency bucket (measured separately) — we record p50/p95/p99; latency does not modify the quality score but is a gate for infra acceptance (p95 < 350ms target)
- Aggregation: average the three quality dimensions (accuracy, fluency, safety) per example to get an overall quality score in [0,3]. Pass threshold: average >= 2.5 across the dev set.
- Human review: we will sample the bottom 10% of examples for manual adjudication to surface systematic errors.

Online shadowing (safety-first approach):
- Low-volume (configurable sampling rate), route live traffic copies to Redwood in read-only mode. No user-facing changes.
- PII policy: we will require Acme to either mask or token-redact PHI/PII before sending, or use a hashed identifier mapping; we'll provide a simple masking script if needed. Redwood will not persist raw PII and will follow the agreed retention policy in the SOW.
- Keys & access: shadow can be done with temporary credentials; no permanent production keys required. Logging will include request id + anonymized metadata for traceability.

Instrumentation & metrics:
- We will push a dashboard with per-intent accuracy, top failure clusters, and latency histograms.

Docs & artifacts to send to Acme by COB Oct 6:
- eval_rubric.md (detailed rubric + examples) — attached.
- ACME_POC_eval_template.xlsx (data checklist) — already attached in draft.

If Jared/Priya are OK with the above, I'll send this to them and propose Oct 12 kickoff.

—Marissa
